quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before you stop.
Let your vehicle slow down before you apply the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. When stopping, ease off the gas pedal first to let your vehicle slow. Then press the brake pedal gently for a smooth stop.

questions.question: You can drive off the road to pass another vehicle:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes going your direction.
Under no circumstances.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: Never drive off the paved road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?

options.text: Yes.
No.
If there is no oncoming traffic.
If the vehicle ahead is driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed. Neither direction can cross these lines, except when turning into or out of a driveway or business entrance.

questions.question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not working due to a power outage:

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat it like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop. When it is your turn, drive through carefully.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Maintain
Vary
Reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning so you can control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and handle unexpected situations.

questions.question: A steady red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Drivers cannot turn in that direction.
Drivers may turn in that direction after a complete stop.
Drivers may turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you cannot go in that direction. You must stop and wait for a green signal.

questions.question: If you need your lights on due to weather or darkness:

options.text: Use your parking lights.
Use your high beams.
Use your low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect light back at you, causing glare and making it harder to see.

questions.question: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead because of low light and glare from other headlights. Always use headlights and drive carefully after dark.

questions.question: Stopping distances and crash severity:

options.text: Decrease as speed increases.
Are not affected by speed.
Increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop and the worse a crash will be.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair driving. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug, whether it is illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
Wait four seconds before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction the arrow points. First, yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: You should check your rearview mirrors:

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors frequently while driving. This helps you know where vehicles are near you. Do not stare in one direction.

questions.question: "No zones" around trucks are areas where cars:

options.text: Disappear into blind spots or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely.
Have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Have several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Disappear into blind spots or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas where cars cannot be seen by the truck driver or are too close to the truck. When a car is in a "no zone," the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely. This greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: This sign warns of a:

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn drivers of upcoming hazards or special conditions. Round signs warn only about railroad crossings ahead.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Lowers your blood alcohol concentration.
Removes the effect of alcohol.
Does not change your blood alcohol concentration.
Raises your blood alcohol concentration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Coffee will not lower your blood alcohol level. It may help keep you awake, but it cannot change how much alcohol is in your body or make you sober.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
Two-way left turn.
Two-way traffic.
Minimum speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: One-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers the direction traffic moves on a one-way street. Drivers must follow this rule.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. Slow down as you approach the intersection. Let any vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection go first. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: If your tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold your steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly during a blowout. Grip the steering wheel tightly to stay in your lane. Slowly release the accelerator and ease off the brakes. When you are moving slowly, gently brake and pull off the road to a safe area.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass even if it is dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
You may not pass.
You may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. A dashed white line can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: The only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration is:

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait and let your body break down the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait and let your body break down the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Time is the only way to lower your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers will not work. They may help you stay awake, but they cannot change your blood alcohol level or make you sober.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on icy or snowy roads to avoid crashes?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave the highways as soon as you can.
Turn on four-wheel drive.
Drive slower and stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower and stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snow or ice. Driving slower and keeping more space between you and other cars are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: When driving near large trucks, what must other drivers plan for?

options.text: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
Large trucks need less distance to stop.
Large trucks are quieter.
Large trucks go faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you. Do not let the truck block your view of the road.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing a car?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to move back.
When you signal for three seconds.
When you see the other car's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the other car's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you are far enough ahead before moving back. Check your rearview mirror. When you see both headlights of the car you passed, you have enough space to return to your lane safely.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street in the wrong direction.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Cars turning left on green must wait for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars turning left on green must wait for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign works with a traffic light. It tells drivers turning left that they do not have the right-of-way. They must wait for oncoming traffic to pass first.

questions.question: What must you do when you hear a fire engine siren behind you?

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Turn on your flashers.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull to the side of the road and stop right away.
